subject: Executive exception request — AcuityHealth starter safeguard
messages:
From: Emma Ross <emma@acuityhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial proposal: Redwood starter retainer + dedicated burst

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a short exec sync and can move quickly if terms are reasonable. High level: AcuityHealth is prepared to commit $420,000 ARR (first 12 months) to Redwood if we can get a package that includes:

- 40% first-year discount on list pricing (applied to usage and seats)
- $50k onboarding/implementation credit to cover integration and a pilot with our SRE team
- Dedicated VPC access with guaranteed burstable capacity for expected traffic spikes (Q3 ramp)
- 12-month minimum commitment, then evaluation for expansion in year 2

We prefer to execute a short LOI this week and get legal/finance working in parallel. I attached a signed LOI for your reference (Acuity_LOI_signed.pdf). Please let me know whether this requires any special approvals on your end — our procurement team wants to close by the end of the month.

Best,
Emma Ross
Head of Platform Partnerships — AcuityHealth
emma@acuityhealth.com

Attachment: Acuity_LOI_signed.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Ross <emma@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Commercial proposal: Redwood starter retainer + dedicated burst — internal approval request

Team — forwarding Acuity's ask. Short version: they want a 40% first-year discount + $50k onboarding credit for a $420k ARR starter retainer and dedicated burst capacity. This exceeds our standard commercial guardrails (25% max on starter pilots). They are strategic: health vertical, potential multi-product expansion (NLP templates + private deployments) and competitive risk if we decline.

Requesting VP/CFO-level exception to:
- Approve 38% first-year discount (compromise) OR up to 40% if we get a 24-month commit
- Approve $50k onboarding credit (can be amortized over 12 months)
- Approve dedicated VPC burst at published rates with a capped credit applied for first 3 months

I've attached a one-page commercial exception memo with ARR math, margin impact, and upsell plan (acuity_commercial_exception_memo.pdf). Key justifications:
- $420k ARR immediate revenue, referenceability in healthcare vertical
- 3x expansion potential in 18 months per product lead signals
- Competitor (XPS) is in active procurement with them; losing this helps the competitor land a strong health customer

Questions for execs: margin hit tolerance, precedent okay for similar deals, and whether we want to condition with a product SLA/fallback that reverts pricing if usage doesn't meet thresholds.

Please reply with: APPROVE / APPROVE W/ FINANCE CONDITIONS / DENY. If APPROVE, we need Marissa to route to CFO for signoff and a DocuSign ready contract pulled by Legal.

Thanks — I can hop on a 15-min call.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Commercial proposal: Redwood starter retainer + dedicated burst — internal approval request

Karthik — thanks for the memo and the attached LOI. Quick financial read:

- Baseline ARR: $420k
- Proposed 40% discount => first-year net revenue ~ $252k
- $50k onboarding credit reduces recognized cash in year 1 further (net ~ $202k realized, ignoring deferred accounting nuances)

This is a material margin hit relative to our standard pilot economics. I'm open to a concession but prefer the following counter that preserves economics and reduces precedent risk:

Counter proposal to present to Acuity:
- 25% first-year discount (within guardrails) + $30k onboarding credit
- 12-month minimum commitment remains; add a 9-month price floor (guaranteed minimum spend)
- Include a clear expansion milestone: if Acuity hits X usage/throughput milestone within 9 months, we automatically convert an incremental credit to expansion discount and review a dedicated capacity uplift at published rates

If leadership wants to go deeper on discount (up to ~35–38%), I will need explicit CFO signoff and a write-up on precedent and margin remediation (e.g., marketing/PS co-fund or deferred revenue recognition).

Markus — leaving to you for commercial / strategic view.

– Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Commercial proposal: Redwood starter retainer + dedicated burst — internal approval request

Appreciate the concise memo, Karthik. Strategic note: Acuity is a high-value reference in healthcare (they buy into security posture and long-term private deployment). I support making a commercial concession with guardrails. My conditional approval:

- Approve up to 35% first-year discount (not to exceed $420k threshold without explicit CFO signoff)
- Approve $40k onboarding credit (cap the PS credit)
- Require a 12-month contractual minimum + a 9-month usage milestone; add an opt-out clause that reverts pricing if usage is < 40% of forecast after 9 months

Marissa — please prepare a short CFO packet summarizing margin impact and precedent, and route to Finance/CFO for final signoff. If CFO declines, revert to Marissa's counter above for Karthik to present.

Karthik — please prepare a one-pager with: ARR math, competitor risk, and proposed milestone metrics (usage, seats, SLA). I want to see the uplift trajectory before final DocuSign.

Markus
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exec exception request — AcuityHealth (deal ACU-2027-58) — memo and LOI attached for CFO routing

Marissa — per Markus, attaching the updated one-pager and the signed LOI for routing to CFO. I drafted a short justification for Finance:

- Commercial impact: list $420k ARR; first-year net revenue under Markus' conditional (35% discount + $40k PS credit) => net ~ $245k gross; with $40k credit realized net ≈ $205k in year 1; 18–36 month expansion potential estimated at +$1.2M (product cross-sell).
- Strategic urgency: competitor actively in procurement; losing this would likely delay healthcare go-to-market by 6–12 months for us.
- Risk mitigation: price reversion clause if usage < 40% of forecast at 9 months; PS credit amortized over 12 months; require Legal to add rollback language.

Attachments: acuity_commercial_exception_memo.pdf, Acuity_LOI_signed.pdf (forwarded). Please route to CFO and loop in Legal if CFO wants to proceed; I can be on any follow-up call this afternoon. If CFO approves, I'll finalize the DocuSign and request Legal to apply the rollback SLA clause.

Thanks — Karthik
Account Executive, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
